note: Engine wrote Latin for many of his lines (Ayan, aju, heret, nadabet); trust Amal's echoes (40:30 عجا = aja). Names: Palestine, Adam = Amsterdam (الإدام 51:20), أمريكا are names, not vocab. D3 and D10 are the same sky moment - one row (D10).

row.why: He dropped على after دير بالي again ~2 min after A7; Amal named the rule ('بدير بالي takes على') and he said ديرت بالي على ختيفتي at 11:50. A separate moment: she fixed it a second time, not a GR-28 repeat (>30 s later).
row.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rulings.why: Real, second voiced fix of the same rule, separate from A7.
Cannot be verified: 'راح عمله' is ra7 a3mlo with the a- of أعمله run into راح in speech; the engine drops the hamza. S4 sound/engine, no signal from Amal.
Duplicate of D10 (the sky didn't-know at 16:33-16:35). His guess أسف (عصفور) was a question he himself rejected at 16:04 ('No. That's bird'); the one row is the word Amal supplied, سما.

row.medi_said: الـ سما بي الليل بي قمر. الـ قمر. الـ قمر.
row.why: After في (there is) the new noun takes no el-; he first said بي قمر (right) then switched to الـ قمر; Amal said قمر twice over him but he kept الـ قمر at 22:09 - unclear if her قمر was a recast or an echo of 22:03, so B / low.
row.english: In the sky at night there is a moon.

rulings.why: Existential في takes an indefinite noun; Amal's قمر may be a recast but it is not clear, so grammar-B low.
A question about the form ('is the verb بمطر؟') is neither a slip nor a use; at 29:54 he says the verb is always feminine, so the engine's بمطر at 29:47 is most likely بتمطر misheard.

row.medi_said: Il hawa aju ktir il sabah
row.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟ ... Tell me it was very strong. The wind was very strong in the mornings.
row.why: Engine wrote aju; Amal's echo عجا كتير shows he said aja (singular), so no number slip. The error is the wrong verb: اجا (came) for the wind being strong; she did not understand ('إيش يعني') and gave the English rephrase 'it was very strong'; he then said il hawa kaan awi ktir.
row.english: The wind was very strong this morning.

rulings.why: Trust Amal's echo عجا (singular), so not B18; the fix she voiced is the word choice -> vocab-A tier 1.

row.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
row.why: He used في (there is) as the verb 'is' in 'his favorite book isn't here'; Amal named the rule 'في is not is, في is there is' - Arabic needs no 'to be': just مش هون. He took it ('مش هون. Okay, you're right').

rulings.why: Amal named a grammar rule (no word for 'is'), so grammar C1, not vocab.

Cannot be verified - transcript hole: 'Lisa hom shob. Lisa kamara.' is a Latin engine garble; Amal repeated her question (she likely did not hear him) and gave no fix; 'hom' cannot be shown to be a pronoun he said.

row.medi_said: الدرس إنه إنتي... / خلينا نعمل الدرس إنه، تفتتلي.
row.why: He said twice (14:42, 15:00) 'the lesson that you planned' (his own English at 15:13) with إنه instead of اللي; Amal's كيف يعني؟ was about تفتتلي (A10), not the relative word, so she let it pass.
row.english: Let's do the lesson that you planned.

rulings.why: Real relative-clause slip she did not address.

row.why: He could not recall sky (guessed أسف = عصفور, 'No. That's bird'); Amal supplied سما. Sheet: 'sky | Sama | سما'.

rulings.why: Didn't-know, Amal supplied the word; absorbs D3.
Engine/sound: 'نسيت تلك' runs the final ت into the ت of تلك, so نسي is the engine; he says نسيتو / نسيته correctly at 16:33 and 22:48. The same line's real slip is A13 (تلك).
Sound shape only (missing doubled ل, F3 family, not scored): Amal said ممتاز to the same تلجات at 35:27 and at 36:58; her تَلَّجَت recast only adds the shadda - S4.

He started the right word (بـ ح... = بحرق; engine wrote به / بهدئ) and she finished it - help on the way to a right answer; he then used it himself ('bit behre', 44:08). Not provable as a didn't-know.

row.amal_said: I don't know. صخر is under the sea, under the ocean.
row.why: Amal asked 'طيب rocks', he said ما بعرف, and she supplied صخر. Sheet: 'rock | Sa5ra | صخرة'.

rulings.why: Closing courtesy exchange, not a fix: he answered with a form of الله يعافيكي and Amal replied يعطيك العافية as her own goodbye; no correction signal.

challenges.why: Not a speaking slip: he mistranslated Amal's question امتى الشمس بتطلع؟ as 'when do you watch the sky?' - he misread her Arabic, so it should be mode = listening (kept apart), not a speaking vocab-A.
Amal accepted واحدة شمس ('Mm-hmm. واحدة. Great job.') - fine as grammar-B, but she clearly did not correct it; check it is never scored as a voiced fix.
